From the owner
Eichler Remodel Series #2: Bringing Back the Beauty of Philippine Mahogany! How do you remodel a classic Eichler home without losing the character that makes it special? Sometimes, you have to turn back the clock! In our recently completed whole-home Eichler remodel in Palo Alto's Greenmeadow neighborhood, one of our favorite challenges was recreating the home's original Philippine Mahogany (Luan) wall paneling. Joseph Eichler's mid-century modern homes are famous for their clean lines, open floor plans, and beautiful wood finishes. But matching those original finishes more than 60 years later? That's where craftsmanship meets detective work! Our team at The Kitchen and Bath Company of Palo Alto went beyond simply installing new paneling. We recreated the original wood finishes, developed a custom period-correct stain to match the vintage paneling, and fabricated the distinctive rounded wood corners (quarter rounds) that helped give these homes their signature look. Fun Eichler Fact: Many original Eichler interiors featured thin Philippine Mahogany plywood paneling, giving the homes their warm, natural appearance. Preserving that look is part of preserving Palo Alto's architectural history. The result? Modern improvements that respect the home's mid-century roots. Next in our Eichler Remodel Series: More behind-the-scenes details from this complete home transformation!

From the owner
Kitchen remodel cost is not a fixed number - it is a variable, and one of its most powerful drivers is timing. Two seasons stand out clearly. Late fall and winter - November, December, January, and February - bring the lowest cost pressure. Contractors have more scheduling flexibility during these months. Spring is the opposite. Demand rises sharply in April and May. Contractor schedules fill quickly. Off-peak timing in Dallas can reduce contractor costs by 5-15%, but those savings aren’t automatic. Getting quotes from at least three contractors during these off-peak windows strengthens your position further. You can lock in pricing now even if work starts later. Signing early captures lower rates before contractor calendars fill up. The most common mistake is waiting until you are ready to start before reaching out to contractors. This eliminates negotiation leverage and forces peak-season pricing regardless of your preferred start month. The sequence - not just the season - determines what you pay.
